extracted.intended_audience: NIAID intramural scientists and supporting administrative staff (division contacts, extramural program staff, TTIPO, Office of Ethics, grants management, acquisitions)
extracted.subtask_description: Standard operating procedure for NIAID intramural scientists initiating or participating in collaborations with extramural investigators on grants and contracts, and for the NIAID staff who review, approve, and manage those collaborations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Early consultation before agreeing to collaboration
rubrics_metrics.description: As soon as possible, before agreeing to a collaboration with an extramural investigator, do the following: Discuss the proposed collaboration with your representative in NIAID's Technology Transfer and Intellectual Property Office (TTIPO); your division contact (DCR—John Tierney; DIR—your laboratory’s SOM or lab operations coordinator; VRC—Judy Stein); NIAID's Office of Extramural Research Policy and Operations (OERPO)—DEA Policy Shop; NIAID’s Office of Acquisitions (OA) if your collaboration involves an extramural contract—Merrill Foster.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Initiate these discussions early to identify issues (ethics, IP, conflicts, material transfer) before committing to the collaboration. The SOP frames this as a required preparatory step.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on using NIH grant/contract funds for intramural activities
rubrics_metrics.description: NIH grant or contract funds cannot be used to support any aspect of intramural activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Extramural scientists working in intramural labs may bring their own resources even if those supplies and materials were purchased with grant or contract funds. If the collaboration would bring money or property to your lab or NIAID, follow the 'Outside Funding for Intramural Investigators' instructions for approval.

rubrics_metrics.name: Complete and route formal letter of collaboration
rubrics_metrics.description: Complete this formal letter of collaboration template and send it to your intramural division contact. Put the letter on DHHS letterhead. Sign the finalized letter. Your division contact will gather additional signatures and negotiate potential changes as necessary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After you receive the required signatures, send copies of the collaboration letter to a specified set of recipients (lab chief, TTIPO contact, division director, named DCR/DIR/VRC contacts, DEA, Office of Ethics, Acting Deputy Director of Science Management and Operations). Division contact is responsible for shepherding the letter through reviews and signature collection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cannot join project until intramural division director approval
rubrics_metrics.description: Notify your collaborator that you cannot join the project until you receive approval from your intramural division director.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While waiting to hear whether your collaboration is approved, you may write the application and prepare to apply, but you must not consider yourself an approved participant until the intramural division director signs off.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ensure solicitation/resource availability for contracts
rubrics_metrics.description: If the proposed collaboration involves an extramural contract, ensure the solicitation states that the resource is available to all offerors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This prevents exclusive advantage from intramural resources; Office of Acquisitions and contracting officers should be engaged to reflect shared-resource availability in solicitations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intramural Division Contact responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: Guide intramural investigators through the collaboration documentation, review, and approval process. Advise intramural investigators on: OE and TTIPO reviews; standards of conduct; material transfer; approval process; appropriateness of the solicitation or funding opportunity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Send draft collaboration letters to TTIPO for review; resolve any conflicts identified by TTIPO or OE; review the collaboration letter to ensure recommended changes have been incorporated; obtain the intramural scientist's and scientific director's signature for approval; send a copy of the signed letter to TTIPO and OE.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extramural Program Staff responsibilities and restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: If an intramural scientist wants to collaborate with an extramural grant recipient, discuss the nature of the collaboration with the intramural scientist and supervisor. If the collaboration involves a grant, indicate in the Program Officer Checklist in eRA whether an intramural staff person is substantially involved in the research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the collaboration involves a contract: notify your contracting officer; work with the contracting officer to make all shared resources available to all offerors; refer all communications with potential offerors to the contracting officer. Do not discuss the review or award status of an application or proposal that involves an intramural collaboration with anybody. Intramural scientists must communicate directly with their collaborators. Applicants and offerors may refuse to release information. Never broker a deal on your own; the intramural lab chief and scientific director will determine, review, and approve the extent and nature of any collaboration.

rubrics_metrics.name: TTIPO review and agreement determination
rubrics_metrics.description: Receive all inquiries concerning collaborations from the intramural division contact or directly from the scientists involved. Determine whether a Material Transfer Agreement, Cooperative Research and Development Agreement, or other agreement is required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the collaboration involves applying for nonfederal grants, receiving grants from other federal agencies, or accepting gifts, follow the procedures at 'Obtaining Approval To Accept Conditional Gifts.' Establish appropriate internal controls for reviewing and reporting collaborations to the Office of Science Management and Operations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Office of Ethics review and conflict-of-interest clearance
rubrics_metrics.description: Review copies of draft letters of collaboration to ensure there are no conflict of interest or ethics issues. Identify, negotiate, provide options, and resolve any issues identified with proposed collaborations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure that none of the conflict of interest or ethics issues outlined in 'Participation of NIH Staff in Extramural Grants—Conflict of Interest and Ethical Considerations' exist or are anticipated at the time of the proposed collaboration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program Officer Checklist & substantial involvement reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: If the collaboration involves a grant, indicate in the Program Officer Checklist located in eRA’s Program Management Module whether an intramural staff person is substantially involved in the research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This checkbox/notation triggers downstream review by grants management and may affect award terms (e.g., conversion to cooperative agreement). Accurate reporting in eRA is required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grants management: cooperative agreement conversion and funding restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: Consult NIH Policy Manual, Chapter 4202-203—Implementation of Cooperative Agreements for policy on intramural collaboration that may require funding the research as a cooperative agreement. Policy that an intramural scientist may not receive extramural funds to participate in a cooperative agreement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the Program Officer Checklist indicates that an intramural staff person is substantially involved in the research, bring this to the attention of the Chief Grants Management Officer. The Chief Grants Management Officer will determine if the grant needs to be converted to a cooperative agreement. If intramural scientists are involved as collaborators in extramural research, add a special term to the Notice of Award that restricts the transfer directly or indirectly of extramural funds (such as salary, travel, equipment) to the intramural lab.

rubrics_metrics.name: Office of Acquisitions contract-file and Advance Understandings requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: If a contract involves intramural resources, make sure the solicitation states that these resources are available to all offerors. If intramural scientists are collaborators on a contract, include: copy of the scientific director’s approval in the contract file; statement in the Summary of Negotiations that terms and conditions have been added to the Advance Understandings Article of the contract restricting the transfer of extramural funds to the intramural lab.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In the Advance Understandings Article, include terms and conditions that restrict the transfer directly or indirectly of extramural funds (such as salary, travel, equipment) to the intramural lab. Office of Acquisitions staff should advise investigators, program officers, and extramural scientists on resources, funding, or personnel matters relating to a contract.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distribution of signed collaboration letter to required contacts
rubrics_metrics.description: After you receive the required signatures, send copies of the collaboration letter to the following people: Your lab chief; Your TTIPO contact; Your division director; DCR—Tara Palmore; DIR—Steven M. Holland; VRC—Ted Pierson; Division of Extramural Activities (DEA)—Kelly Poe; Office of Ethics (OE)—Jeremy Tam; NIAID’s Acting Deputy Director of Science Management and Operations—Christopher Hanson.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timely distribution ensures all oversight offices are aware and can complete their reviews/recordkeeping. It documents approvals and supports any downstream grant/contract actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restrictions on discussing review/award status and brokering
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not discuss the review or award status of an application or proposal that involves an intramural collaboration with anybody. Never broker a deal on your own.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refer communications about procurement or offeror information to the contracting officer; intramural lab chief and scientific director determine/approve the nature of collaborations. This preserves procurement integrity and avoids unauthorized commitments.
